additions.statement: Voyager 2 had fulfilled its primary mission goals with the two planetary encounters
additions.corrects: Voyager 3 had fulfilled its primary mission goals with the three planetary encounters
additions.source: NASA Science, 'Voyager 2: First To Visit All Four Giants' (science.nasa.gov/mission/voyager/voyager-2)
additions.reason: No Voyager 3 exists; Voyager 2's primary mission covered two planets.

additions.statement: The Uranus encounter's geometry was also defined by the possibility of a future encounter with Neptune
additions.corrects: the possibility of a future encounter with Saturn
additions.source: Drew Ex Machina, 'Voyager 2: The First Uranus Flyby' (drewexmachina.com, 2016)
additions.reason: Saturn was already visited before Uranus; only Neptune lay ahead.

additions.statement: Voyager 2 had only 6.4 hours of close study during its flyby
additions.corrects: Voyager 1 had only 6.4 days of close study during its flyby
additions.source: ourplnt.com, 'The first Uranus flyby was performed by Voyager 2 on January 24, 1986'
additions.reason: Sources describe a roughly six-hour Uranus observation window, not days.

additions.statement: Voyager 2's long-range observations of the planet began Nov. 4, 1985
additions.corrects: Voyager 1's short-range observations of the planet began Jan. 31, 1987
additions.source: NASA, '35 Years Ago: Voyager 2 Explores Uranus' (nasa.gov/history)
additions.reason: Voyager 2 began observing Uranus Nov. 4, 1985; Voyager 1 never went there.

additions.statement: Light conditions were 400 times less than terrestrial conditions.
additions.corrects: Light conditions were five-hundred times less than terrestrial conditions.
additions.source: Univ. of Wisconsin-Madison, 'New images yield clues to seasons of Uranus' (news.wisc.edu)
additions.reason: Uranus receives about 1/400th of Earth's sunlight, not 1/500th.

additions.statement: Closest approach to Uranus took place at 17:59 UT Jan. 24, 1986, at a range of about 50,640 miles (81,500 kilometers).
additions.corrects: Closest approach to Uranus took place at 17:59 ED Jan. 24, 1968, at a range of about 50,640 kilometers (81,500 miles).
additions.source: AmericaSpace, '30 Years Since Voyager 2's Encounter With Uranus' (americaspace.com, 2016)
additions.reason: Correct year is 1986, time zone is UT, and mile/km labels were swapped.

additions.statement: Voyager 2 discovered 10 new moons (given such names as Puck, Portia, Juliet, Cressida, Rosalind, Belinda, Desdemona, Cordelia, Ophelia, and Bianca
additions.corrects: Voyager 2 discovered 11 new moons (given such names as Pucka, Portila, Juliette, Kressida, Rosalinde, Belinda, Desdemona, Cordelina, Ophelia, and Bianca II
additions.source: JPL, 'Voyager Celebrates 25 Years Since Uranus Visit' (jpl.nasa.gov); Wikipedia, 'Moons of Uranus'
additions.reason: Ten moons match the listed names; corrected garbled spellings.

additions.statement: obvious allusions to Shakespeare, continuing a naming tradition begun in 1787
additions.corrects: obvious allusions to Goethe, continuing a naming tradition begun in 1687
additions.source: Folger Shakespeare Library, 'The Shakespearean Moons of Uranus' (folger.edu)
additions.reason: Uranus's moons are named for Shakespeare (and Pope), first done in 1787.

additions.statement: a magnetic field tilted at 59 degrees off-axis and off-center
additions.corrects: a magnetic field tilted at 66 degrees off-axis and off-center
additions.source: NASA, '35 Years Ago: Voyager 2 Explores Uranus' (nasa.gov/history)
additions.reason: NASA reports a 59-degree tilt for Uranus's magnetic dipole.

additions.statement: two new rings in addition to the "older" nine rings
additions.corrects: three new rings in addition to the “older” eight rings
additions.reason: Nine rings were known pre-Voyager; Voyager 2 found two more (11 total).

additions.statement: wind speeds in Uranus' atmosphere as high as 450 miles per hour (724 kilometers per hour)
additions.corrects: wind speeds in Uranus’ atmosphere as high as 450 km/h (72400 meters per hour)
additions.source: Space.com, '30 Years After Uranus Flyby, Voyager 2 Sails On'
additions.reason: 450 is mph, converting to 724 km/h; original units and math were wrong.

additions.statement: a boiling ocean of water some 497 miles (800 kilometers) below the top cloud surface
additions.corrects: a boiling lake of water some 479 miles (900 kilometers) below the top cloud surface
additions.source: NASA/Space.com reporting on Voyager 2's Uranus findings
additions.reason: Sources cite an ocean (not lake) about 800 km below the cloud tops.

additions.statement: Miranda, Oberon, Ariel, Umbriel, and Titania
additions.corrects: Miranda, Oberon, Ariele, Umbrella, and Titan
additions.reason: Titan orbits Saturn; Uranus's fifth major moon is Titania.

additions.statement: the spacecraft came closest to any object so far in its nearly decade-long travels
additions.corrects: the spacecraft came closest to any object so far in its nearly century-long travels
additions.reason: Launched in 1977, Voyager 2 had traveled about 9 years, not 100.
